findings.summary: Task 1 adds the platforms key but leaves the repository-wide check red until the documentation task.
findings.evidence: Brief Shape lines 416-418 place the key in task 1 and lines 430-433 put its configuration-guide entry in task 5. .vloop/config.toml's only check applies to paths ["**"] and runs go run ./tools/check. internal/cli/guide_test.go:135-144 and internal/cli/commands_doc_test.go:41-50 require every config.Keys entry, including its VLOOP_* name, to appear in docs/guide/configuration.md. Adding platforms to config.Keys in task 1 therefore makes the after-task-1 check fail before task 5.
findings.fix: Put the minimal platforms key and VLOOP_PLATFORMS entries in task 1, or move the complete configuration-guide task before the key is added, so the permanent check is green after every task.

findings.summary: Task 5 requires a work session to edit .vloop/config.toml, which the loop forbids.
findings.evidence: Brief M5 at lines 272-273 and Shape task 5 at lines 430-433 require .vloop/config.toml to add platforms. Domain S-4 at docs/domain/domain-model.md:220 allows no work-session writes under .vloop except .vloop/tmp, and fence/work.json:79-80 explicitly denies Edit(.vloop/config.toml) and Write(.vloop/config.toml). The task therefore cannot be completed by a loop session.
findings.fix: Move the repository config edit to the ready commit or to a named operator step outside the loop, and make task 5 verify the resulting configuration rather than require the work session to write it.

findings.section: M4 — gate shell and Decided here
findings.summary: The gate-shell rule says mixed teams always check configured pwsh even with a plan, but P-5 makes an already accepted plan's shell authoritative.
findings.evidence: Brief M4 lines 238-241 requires the configured pwsh row to be a problem with or without a plan. The same brief at lines 281-282 says an accepted plan keeps its shell and does not re-check gates when platforms is added later, while docs/domain/domain-model.md:202-203 (P-5) says the plan's shell governs from then on. internal/cli/doctor.go:474-492 currently checks plan.Shell whenever a plan exists. A pre-mixed plan can therefore legitimately use sh while config requires pwsh.
findings.fix: State the precedence literally: an accepted plan's recorded shell governs its gate-shell row and gates; mixed-team pwsh enforcement applies to config, doctor without an in-use plan, and the next plan.

decisions: Shared-only errors apply to every command that reads config, not only run: approve; this follows B39's treatment of a local [[check]].
An accepted plan keeps its shell and is not re-linted when platforms appears later: approve P-5 preservation, but M4 must state its scope as noted above.
vloop task verify is not portability-linted: approve and keep it explicitly outside this run's scope.
The automatic lint reads .ps1 files only, while other gate-script languages are judged through their verify command or the skills: approve, with the resulting limitation already stated.
